question.text: An investor wants to invest in mutual funds without routing the investment through a distributor. Which of the following options is most suitable?

answer.text: Investing through a bank's mutual fund desk using their ARN
Investing directly through the AMC's website or app in a Direct Plan
Investing through an individual distributor who charges a separate advisory fee
Investing through a stock broker who routes orders via BSE StAR MF using an ARN

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A (p.120), AMC-created web/mobile platforms allow the investor to deal directly with the mutual fund. Per p.166, Direct Plans are designed for investors who purchase units directly from the fund without routing through a distributor; per p.174 and p.177, the application form treatment distinguishes Direct from Regular Plans on this basis. The Trap: Option A involves a bank acting as distributor (with ARN), so the investment is routed through a distributor. Option C still involves a distributor. Option D routes the order through an ARN-holding intermediary. Only investing directly with the AMC in a Direct Plan removes the distributor leg. Note: "Regular Plan" applies where the investment is routed through a distributor and the distributor's ARN is recorded against the folio; "Direct Plan" applies where it is not.
